name: Nathanael
role: Disciple from Cana whom Jesus saw under the fig tree
whenBasis: Jesus' ministry, from the fifteenth year of Tiberius (Luke 3:1), AD 28–29, to the crucifixion under Pilate, AD 30 or 33 on reckonings from the gospels' weekday.
summary: A man of Cana in Galilee whom Philip brought to Jesus. Told they had found the one Moses wrote about, Jesus of Nazareth, he asked, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Jesus called him a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit, and said he had seen him under the fig tree before Philip called him. Nathanael answered, “Rabbi… You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
body: Jesus promises he will see greater things: heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man. He is among the seven disciples fishing on the Sea of Tiberias when the risen Jesus appears on the shore.

later.text: The other gospels never name him, and John never names Bartholomew. Johann Bengel takes the two to be one man, Bartholomew being a name from his father (son of Tolmai) as Bar-Jona is Simon's, since Matthew pairs Bartholomew with Philip and John 21:2 places Nathanael among the apostles. Alfred Plummer reports the identification as common and gives five reasons for it, but holds that they make it no more than probable, and notes that the framers of the Anglican liturgy did not set this passage for St Bartholomew's Day.

sources.title: Gnomon of the New Testament, on John 1:45
sources.author: J. A. Bengel
sources.note: tr.: 'It is probable that he was admitted among the apostles, and that he was the same person as he who is called Bartholomew, by a secondary name derived from his father'

sources.title: The Gospel According to S. John (Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges)
sources.author: A. Plummer
sources.note: on 1:45: 'Nathanael is commonly identified with Bartholomew … But all these reasons do not make the identification more than probable.'

traditions: no more than probable: Alfred Plummer
